input: Compile a contact list for freelance client outreach

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: The type of freelance work determines which industries and roles to target — a copywriter's list looks nothing like a web developer's.
Knowing the specific decision-maker to contact (e.g. marketing manager vs. founder vs. HR) shapes what fields the list needs and where to find contacts.
Whether outreach is cold, warm (referrals/past clients), or a mix determines sourcing strategy entirely.
The target number of contacts affects how much time and tooling is needed — 20 vs. 500 contacts are very different projects.
The format and tool (spreadsheet, CRM, Notion, etc.) affects how the list is structured and what columns to include.
Geographic or niche focus (local businesses, startups, enterprise, specific country) narrows sourcing and affects messaging relevance.
Knowing what a 'good' contact entry looks like — just a name and email vs. enriched data like LinkedIn URL, company size, notes — defines the depth of research needed.

gold.taskTitle: Compile a freelance client outreach contact list
gold.taskDescription: Build a structured list of potential clients to contact for freelance work outreach.

questions.title: What type of freelance work are you seeking clients for?
questions.description: Identify the freelance service or skill (e.g. graphic design, copywriting, software development) to ensure contacts are sourced from the right industries and roles.

questions.title: Which specific job title or role should you contact?
questions.description: Determine the decision-maker persona to target (e.g. founder, marketing manager, creative director) so the list captures the right person at each company.

questions.title: Are these cold leads, warm contacts, or both?
questions.description: Clarify whether outreach targets brand-new prospects, existing connections or past clients, or a combination, as this drives where and how contacts are sourced.

questions.title: How many contacts do you need to compile?
questions.description: Establish a target volume so the effort, tooling, and time required can be scoped appropriately.

questions.title: What tool or format should the list be built in?
questions.description: Determine whether the list will live in a spreadsheet, CRM, Notion, Airtable, or another tool to define structure and required fields up front.

questions.title: Is there a geographic or industry niche to focus on?
questions.description: Identify any location, sector, or company-size filters (e.g. local SMEs, US-based SaaS startups) to narrow sourcing and keep outreach relevant.

questions.title: What data fields must each contact entry include?
questions.description: Define the minimum required information per contact (e.g. name and email only vs. enriched with LinkedIn, company size, and personalisation notes) to set the research depth.
